exposure: Thrombocytopenia in pregnancy (causes: Gestational Thrombocytopenia (GT), Hypertensive Disorders in Pregnancy (HDP), Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP))
outcome: Maternal laboratory indexes (e.g., platelet count, TEG parameters)
Neonatal birth conditions (e.g., NICU transfer rate, birth weight)
cohort: A total of 151 pregnant women diagnosed with thrombocytopenia were included in the study.
finding: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is associated with more severe thrombocytopenia and bleeding, often presenting early in pregnancy, while hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (HDP) are linked to a higher neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) transfer rate and lower birth weight.
